# Preface {.unnumbered}

*Dedicated to my parents, partner, and children. Thank you for teaching me the true joy of descent with modification.*

This text is released under the Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported License (<http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/>): you are free to reuse and remix this work, but please include an attribution to the original. The Quarto source in this repository was converted automatically from the LaTeX source at <https://github.com/cooplab/popgen-notes>; see `tools/convert.py`.

Author: Graham Coop, Department of Evolution and Ecology & Center for Population Biology, University of California, Davis (`gmcoop@ucdavis.edu`).

This book was developed from my set of notes for the [Population Biology graduate group](http://www-eve.ucdavis.edu/eve/pbg/) core class (PBG200A) and the undergraduate Population and Quantitative Genetics class (EVE102) at UC Davis. Thanks to the many students who've read these notes and suggested improvements. Thanks to Simon Aeschbacher, Vince Buffalo, Erin Calfee, and Michael Whitlock who read and extensively edited earlier drafts of these notes.

To illustrate these notes, I've used old scientific and natural history illustrations, in part because they are out of copyright but mainly because they bring me joy. Many of the old images come from the [Biodiversity Heritage Library](https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/), a consortium of natural history institutions that are digitizing their collections and making them freely available online. If you enjoy the images consider donating to the [BHL](http://library.si.edu/donate-bhl). Many of the data and simulation graphics in the book were prepared in R [@Rstats]; the code for each is linked from the caption of each figure. In many cases data were extracted from old figures using the [WebPlotDigitizer](https://automeris.io/WebPlotDigitizer/) tool, so I advise re-extracting the data if you wish to use it for research purposes.
